text:
Standard GRU reset gates filter the candidate-state computation; update gates control the carry path. An extra gate applied as GRU(x, g⊙h) additionally changes every hidden-dependent computation, so it differs from either gate alone, although usefulness remains unproven. Closest recommendation precedent: T-GRU multiplies only the carry term, h′=z⊙g⊙h+(1−z)⊙candidate, with g conditioned on elapsed time, input and history. Its ablations support temporal gating on several datasets, including Amazon categories, but do not establish benefits for whole-state pre-gating or parameter-matched superiority. Monotonic exponential decay showed no obvious improvement. [T-GRU/MTAM paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2005.08598)

Initialization matters: analytically, an added constant retention gate contributes g^k attenuation along the direct carry path; 0.5^50≈8.9×10⁻¹⁶, whereas 0.99^50≈0.605, before ordinary GRU retention. For a reproducible near-identity initialization, zero the added gate’s weights and set bias=logit(p), explicitly reporting p; finite sigmoid biases cannot produce exact identity. Chrono initialization motivates timescale-dependent gate biases, while subsequent work warns that strong saturation can impede learning and makes timescale selection sensitive. These are initialization principles, not evidence of recommendation gains. [Chrono initialization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11188), [gating analysis](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/gu20a/gu20a-supp.pdf)

Recommended controls: corrected standard GRU; fixed g=1; learned pre-gate; carry-only gate; time-conditioned versus content-only gate; and an actively used, parameter-matched GRU variant. Keep seeds, splits, sampling, optimization and validation protocol identical. Measure gate distributions and cumulative log-retention by history length and time gap; bypass padding updates. These proposed controls distinguish temporal information, extra capacity and destructive attenuation, using one trained network per category.
